problems.stem: How does a capsule-based self-healing material typically work?
options: It permanently prevents all cracks from forming
It stores healing agents that are released when damage ruptures the capsules
It relies only on surface repainting by the user
It repairs only if external welding is applied
problems.explanation: Many self-healing materials use embedded capsules or channels that release a repair agent when damage occurs.

problems.stem: Why are self-healing approaches attractive in fatigue-prone systems?
options: Because repeated micro-damage can accumulate before visible failure
Because fatigue never involves crack growth
Because fatigue problems disappear when structures are painted
Because healing materials remove all need for inspection
problems.explanation: Fatigue often starts with small damage that grows over time, so early repair mechanisms can be valuable.

problems.stem: What is an advantage of microvascular repair networks over one-time healing capsules?
options: They can potentially supply repair agents multiple times
They make the material completely homogeneous
They work only in purely decorative parts
problems.explanation: Microvascular systems can support repeated or more distributed repair, unlike single-use capsules.

problems.stem: What is the best engineering interpretation of resilient design in this context?
options: Designing only for maximum initial strength
Designing systems that can tolerate damage and recover useful function
Assuming repair mechanisms have no cost
problems.explanation: Resilient design considers recovery and continued function, not just initial peak performance.
